name: Bluetooth

claims.claim_text: The practical wired and wireless options for moving data in and out of a small instrument are Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and USB; near-field communication is too slow to serve as a general data path.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well, there's Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and USB
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth Low Energy peripheral publishes a generic attribute table as part of its advertising data, so a host can discover what the device does without the PIN exchange and handshake that classic Bluetooth pairing requires.
claims.quote_verbatim: part of the advertising that, that tells everybody what it can do
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Davidson - Hoodied HP Hijinks

claims.claim_text: The wireless standards split by power and bandwidth: Wi-Fi is generally ruled out on battery life, Bluetooth Low Energy is low bandwidth, and classic Bluetooth offers relatively high bandwidth at the cost of holding a connection open continuously.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth low energy is low bandwidth. Bluetooth is relatively high bandwidth if it has to be connected all the time
claims.episode_title: PCB Mills, SDR and Oscilloscopes - Flaunting Furbelow Fanciness

claims.claim_text: The classic Bluetooth HID profile is a common starting point for a wireless input device because it gives very wide compatibility with existing hosts without a custom driver.
claims.quote_verbatim: The HID profile in particular, it is a perfect launch point for very wide compatibility
claims.speaker: Jeff Rowberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: A pre-built radio module stops being the efficient choice at production volumes of roughly one hundred thousand units a year, above which integrating the equivalent circuit onto the product's own board becomes worthwhile.
claims.quote_verbatim: it starts to become less, less efficient to use a module company like us
claims.speaker: Jeff Rowberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth qualification through the SIG is a voluntary association rather than a government regulation: the 2.4 GHz band itself is unlicensed, and certification is only required if a product is to be presented as Bluetooth.
claims.quote_verbatim: you only have to do their certification thing if you are using Bluetooth officially
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth Low Energy and classic Bluetooth occupy exactly the same spectrum and the same set of channels, BLE using a subset, so a dual-mode device cannot fully use both at once; high-bandwidth serial data or high-quality audio consume most of the available spectrum for an active link.
claims.quote_verbatim: BLE and classic Bluetooth use exactly the same spectrum and even the same set of channels
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: Classic Bluetooth profiles such as serial port and HID are defined by the SIG and handed to the implementer, whereas Bluetooth Low Energy requires the profile to be built by the developer unless the stack supplies one; this is more work but allows a very lightweight profile for a simple sensor.
claims.quote_verbatim: you actually have to build the profile yourself unless it's provided for you as part of the stack you're using
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: Android hardware shipped with Bluetooth Low Energy capability before the operating system exposed it; official platform support arrived with API level 18.
claims.quote_verbatim: add their official support for BLE into API 18
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: Placing a Bluetooth device in non-discoverable mode does not prevent an observer from finding it or monitoring its transmissions.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's possible to discover Bluetooth devices that are non-discoverable
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Monitoring a single Bluetooth channel yields enough information to derive the frequency hopping sequence and then follow the link across the band.
claims.quote_verbatim: derive enough information just by monitoring one channel to figure out what the frequency hopping scheme is
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Research tooling that requires a two-thousand-dollar instrument plus a hardware modification is rarely reproduced; the Ubertooth project was started to replace that approach with a low-cost dedicated receiver that monitors one channel and passes the bits to a computer over USB.
claims.quote_verbatim: buy this $2,000 piece of equipment and then take a soldering iron to it
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth hops across 79 MHz of bandwidth, wider than the instantaneous bandwidth of typical software-defined radio front ends, and the minimum gap between packets is a little over 200 microseconds, which sets the hardware retune budget.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth operates over 79 megahertz of bandwidth
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Where a hopping scheme spans more than the receiver's instantaneous bandwidth, the hopping must be implemented in the radio's own microcontroller: adding USB latency to the host round trip pushes the retune well past the inter-packet gap.
claims.quote_verbatim: you'll probably need to implement your frequency hopping in the microcontroller
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Interview with Michael Ossmann - Gifted Grimgribber Grokker

claims.claim_text: Stacking several radios onto one product looks easy because modules exist for each, but battery life and coexistence dominate: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth cannot both be transmitting at the same instant.
claims.quote_verbatim: when we've got wifi going, we can't have Bluetooth going at the exact same time
claims.speaker: Adam Wolf
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Adam Wolf - Brick & Board Biuners

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth's long specification gestation meant its throughput was already inadequate for its original use case by the time silicon shipped: at around 700 kbit/s a four-megapixel image took about two and a half minutes to reach a printer, against 12 Mbit/s for contemporary USB.
claims.quote_verbatim: it took two and a half minutes to transmit that picture to your printer
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth link is not deterministic, which rules it out for head tracking: a dropped packet leaves the rendering engine with a stale head position and produces a visible error.
claims.quote_verbatim: When you're doing head tracking, you really want a deterministic link
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - Intense Illusion Introduction

claims.claim_text: An open-source Bluetooth stack used in an early smartwatch had originally been written as a user-mode stack for jailbroken phones, illustrating how thin the supply of usable third-party stacks was.
claims.quote_verbatim: That was originally written as a user mode stack for jailbroken iPhones
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Working at a very low layer of the Bluetooth protocol, L2CAP, allowed a watch to communicate with BlackBerry applications, but the same approach gave limited support on Android and none on iOS.
claims.quote_verbatim: Using a very low level portion of the Bluetooth protocol called L2Cap
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Inheriting a module's FCC modular certification is conditional on using one of the antennas the module manufacturer had approved, typically a small set of ceramic chip antennas.
claims.quote_verbatim: to use the modular certification, you need to use one of the pre-approved antennas
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Radio performance was verified per unit rather than per design: after the antenna was assembled the complete watch went into an RF test chamber and its output power was measured, alongside a pressure test of the waterproofing.
claims.quote_verbatim: they put it in an RF test chamber and, and measure the output power
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Replacing a certified Bluetooth module with the equivalent circuit laid out directly on the product's own board delivered a substantial cost saving at the price of certifying the radio afresh, and the respin occupied the electrical engineering team for a long period.
claims.quote_verbatim: we did switch away from using the CAN Bluetooth module to sort of putting the equivalent circuit directly on our own board
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Debugging a device over its own Bluetooth link is of limited use when the defects under investigation are in the Bluetooth stack itself; the technique suits application developers whose code sits above the stack.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of the things that we want to debug are to do with the bluetooth stack
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Before Bluetooth Low Energy, an accessory that wanted to talk to Apple hardware needed an authentication chip; a BLE link bypassed that requirement, and even a slow serial channel was sufficient for many accessories.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth allows you to go right past that and just kind of make something that can talk to it
claims.episode_title: Specialized and/or Open Source Test Gear and Dev Boards - Vacation Videography Vorboten

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth devices marketed as internet-connected are in practice phone-connected: a bridging device is required because a Bluetooth peripheral cannot reach the internet on its own.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're really not. They're phone connected devices
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Brandon Harris - Impish Internet Iamatology

claims.claim_text: An FCC compliance failure at the test house came from a classification error rather than a technical fault: a laboratory employee assessed a Bluetooth module against Wi-Fi transmitter criteria.
claims.quote_verbatim: started classifying it as a Wi-Fi transmitter
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Partitioning a low-power design so the radio module maintains the connection while the application microcontroller sleeps lets an infrequent-transmission product keep a live link without keeping the processor awake.
claims.quote_verbatim: the module kind of handles the connection to the iPhone and keeps that established
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Apple implemented Bluetooth Low Energy features that were not in the specification, and the SIG subsequently added them; one example was allowing a phone application to scan for peripherals and to act as a peripheral itself, both at once.
claims.quote_verbatim: they disregarded the Bluetooth spec and actually added features that weren't in the Bluetooth spec
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Because a phone can be made to advertise as a peripheral, hardware can be simulated in software during development, giving a debugging path before the device exists.
claims.quote_verbatim: scans for peripherals or you can write an app that becomes a peripheral
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Android had no standard Bluetooth Low Energy interface until version 4.3; before that a developer had to use each handset manufacturer's own stack, which is why small teams targeted iOS first.
claims.quote_verbatim: you'd have to use the manufacturer-specific stack for each phone. 4.3 added it
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Keeping a radio module and a swappable application coprocessor as separate parts lets prototype firmware move onto a production board of any shape: the same module and protocol are retained while the coprocessor is chosen for cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: just add a different coprocessor, which could be a mega, it could be an MSP430
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Native Bluetooth Low Energy support in both Android and iOS makes the smartphone the default gateway for a sensor: the sensor connects to the phone, and the phone provides display and the path to the cloud.
claims.quote_verbatim: both Android and iOS support Bluetooth low energy natively
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: Before committing to a connected consumer device, the design question is whether the product is really a sensor connecting over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi to a phone or tablet the buyer already owns, which avoids the cost of a custom screen and enclosure at low volume.
claims.quote_verbatim: are you sure this isn't just a sensor connecting over Bluetooth or wifi
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Fixing the reporting interval from assumption rather than from users can dominate a power budget by orders of magnitude: a sensor assumed to need a reading every minute in fact satisfied its users at four readings a day, a roughly thousandfold reduction in energy.
claims.quote_verbatim: the power load for that is drastically less
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: The Bluetooth Smart branding is a compatibility mark rather than a protocol: it indicates a dual-mode device able to work with both classic Bluetooth and Bluetooth Low Energy.
claims.quote_verbatim: It indicates a dual mode device compatible with both classic and low energy

claims.claim_text: The ESP32 places two 240 MHz 32-bit cores running FreeRTOS alongside classic Bluetooth, Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi on a single low-cost chip; at launch its Bluetooth side was effectively undocumented and had to be worked out from forum sample code.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't think the Bluetooth is really documented at this point
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: Early Bluetooth was a multi-chip solution: one company supplied the radio front end, another implemented the baseband in an FPGA or other digital logic, and a large software stack sat above both. Present-day parts integrate all three.
claims.quote_verbatim: we were only doing the radio frequency thing there and, uh, other companies would then do the, the baseband implementation
claims.speaker: Jorgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: Frequency hopping imposes a hard requirement on the synthesiser: the PLL must acquire and lock a new frequency fast enough to be ready for each hop.
claims.quote_verbatim: You need to have a very fast frequency shift system
claims.speaker: Jorgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: The Bluetooth specification continues to branch after two decades; the low-power audio profiles were driven into it by the hearing aid industry and were then available to other industries to build on.
claims.quote_verbatim: this was a big push from the hearing aid industry trying to put some low power audio profiles into there
claims.speaker: Jorgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: An attacker need not extract a cryptographic key from a token: adding a Bluetooth radio to the device and reading and broadcasting the displayed code achieves the same result.
claims.quote_verbatim: let's just add Bluetooth to the device and read the display

claims.claim_text: Early Bluetooth car kits carried vulnerabilities that allowed an unauthenticated party to connect to them.
claims.quote_verbatim: in the early days of Bluetooth hacking, there were a lot of vulnerabilities
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Classic Bluetooth was designed as a wireless serial cable replacement and supports serial port emulation that appears as a COM port at driver level; Bluetooth Low Energy's cable-replacement service does not present the same plug-and-play interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not a COM port like you can get on true Bluetooth

claims.claim_text: Each Bluetooth Low Energy implementation differs in practice, so a product must be validated against individual host implementations rather than against the specification alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: Each BLE implementation is a special snowflake

claims.claim_text: Where a product already carries four AA cells, BLE's power advantage buys little and classic Bluetooth would have been the sounder choice; the module can in any case be powered down entirely between sessions and reconnected.
claims.quote_verbatim: BLE is lower power, but we've got four AA batteries in this thing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A radio module cannot be changed late in a programme because the design is already at the test house undergoing FCC compliance testing; the radio choice is effectively frozen at that point.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't just go change your Bluetooth module at the last minute
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth Low Energy earns its place where a device must run for around two years from a single CR2032 coin cell.
claims.quote_verbatim: BLE is great if you're running something from a coin cell
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A single phone can hold simultaneous Bluetooth Low Energy connections to more than one peripheral, though the practical ceiling is imposed by the host implementation.
claims.quote_verbatim: We're talking to two different meters at once

claims.claim_text: Cloning a combined Wi-Fi and Bluetooth system-on-chip is impractical because a clone would have to implement the radio protocols from scratch; complex clone parts are behavioural simulators with an entirely different internal architecture, not copies of the silicon.
claims.quote_verbatim: the complex clones are more like you know simulators than real clones
claims.speaker: Jeroen Domburg

claims.claim_text: Firmware update over Bluetooth was estimated as disproportionate work and abandoned in favour of an SD card, in part because the link is not reliable enough to be depended on for a whole image transfer.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can do it, but it's a crap ton of work
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Over-the-air update requires a second image region: the new image is downloaded, checksummed and stored separately, verified by running it, and only then copied over the previous one, leaving the old slot free for the next update.
claims.quote_verbatim: I did a check sum on firmware B, I stored it into memory

claims.claim_text: Implementing update over Bluetooth forces the entire Bluetooth stack into the bootloader, which is what makes the feature expensive on a part with a small bootloader region.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to add all the Bluetooth crap to the, you know, to the, to the bootloader

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth is a commodity function, so a custom Bluetooth chip is only justified by a specific need such as a required level of integration, a deliberate deviation from the specification, or an unusual power or battery architecture.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth is more of a commodity
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The 2.4 GHz band is already congested, so streaming continuous data over a Bluetooth link, which the protocol was not designed for, is easily interrupted and shows up as corrupt packets.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a pretty busy channel to start with

claims.claim_text: Devices operating at the edge of the Bluetooth specification interoperate with each other but not necessarily with everything else; the practical remedy is to control and define both ends of the link.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes the Bluetooth ain't so standard

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth Low Energy device will run for about a year even from a small CR2032 cell, but classic Bluetooth is better on connection reliability; the choice turns on how often the device transmits and how quickly it must respond.
claims.quote_verbatim: even with a tiny CR2032 battery, you're still going to get a year's life

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth device addresses, like USB vendor identifiers, are issued by a central authority, because guaranteeing a globally unique address requires one.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's also how the Bluetooth standard works. That's also how USB standard works

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth was in the field for close to a decade before it settled enough for high-quality audio to work interoperably, which is offered as the realistic timescale for a complex new interface standard to stabilise.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth was around for probably almost a decade before it sort of became somewhat standardized
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The nRF52 firmware update mechanism is a sound and reasonably secure design, but per-device keying makes fleet updates awkward, and the correct direction of trust is for the device to authenticate the image it receives rather than the reverse.
claims.quote_verbatim: They have a pretty good, pretty secure method of firmware update
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: Classic Bluetooth was power hungry and centred on audio, with a serial port mode as a secondary feature; Bluetooth Low Energy was introduced to address the power problem and was then adopted across handsets and chipsets.
claims.quote_verbatim: old-fashioned Bluetooth was very power hungry

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth link is used to remove the wired connection from a sensitive measurement instrument so it can run from a lithium-ion cell, which is a low-noise supply compared with mains-derived power; the data arrives as a serial port on the computer.
claims.quote_verbatim: another really low noise power source is a lithium ion battery
claims.speaker: Jean Rintoul

claims.claim_text: A silicon vendor's evaluation hardware is typically a ladder rather than one board: a coin-cell-sized form-factor demonstrator, a broken-out reference design, and a full development kit that supports current measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll have a full scale development kit that will allow you to do current measurements
claims.speaker: Kieran O'Leary

claims.claim_text: Internal characterisation boards spend money and area on supply quality that a customer board would not, because the point is to measure the performance of the silicon rather than the performance of the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want to be measuring the performance of the board. You want to be measuring the performance of the silicon
claims.speaker: Kieran O'Leary

claims.claim_text: For a simple one-way broadcast application a plain 2.4 GHz transceiver is preferable to a full protocol such as Bluetooth or ANT, because the nodes never need to transmit back.
claims.quote_verbatim: I wouldn't implement any high level stuff like Bluetooth

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth is a poor choice where distance matters outdoors: 2.4 GHz propagation degrades as humidity rises and the band is loaded by every phone in the vicinity.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth's not great about like distance stuff

claims.claim_text: A wireless standard functions as a suggestion rather than a contract, and large vendors implement variants; conformance to the specification is what maximises the number of devices a product will interoperate with.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want to interact with the largest number of things

claims.claim_text: A commercial 802.15.4 Thread mesh built on nRF52840 nodes was withdrawn after about a year of development because the networks proved too difficult to set up reliably, leaving radio-only node hardware without a mesh to join.
claims.quote_verbatim: after about a year of trying, they said, nope, we're not going to do that anymore

claims.claim_text: An nRF52840 carrying a bootloader alongside the SoftDevice can accept a new firmware image over the air from a phone application, so a sealed enclosure never has to be opened to update it.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can use the NRF Connect app and load a new piece of firmware in there

claims.claim_text: Zephyr is a real-time operating system that originated at Wind River and passed to the Linux Foundation; its attraction for connected devices is that Bluetooth arrives as an included subsystem rather than as low-level calls into an opaque vendor API.
claims.quote_verbatim: implementing Bluetooth is like a hash include instead of a writing low-level interactions with APIs

claims.claim_text: Nordic's SoftDevice is a precompiled binary with a fixed API that occupies a reserved region at the bottom of flash and a portion of RAM, with the bootloader placed at the top of memory; the application must be linked around both.
claims.quote_verbatim: you just basically have to, like, preserve part of your flash and part of your RAM

claims.claim_text: Both the Bluetooth stack and the bootloader must sit in protected memory so that a failed update can still be recovered over the Bluetooth link.
claims.quote_verbatim: even if you goof it up completely, it's still, you can still recover via the Bluetooth

claims.claim_text: Some microcontrollers provide too little protected memory to hold a Bluetooth stack, which rules out recoverable update over Bluetooth on those parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: Some processors only have that a small amount of protected memory space

claims.claim_text: Firmware update over Bluetooth changes the support economics of a product: an image can be sent to a user and loaded from a phone application without any cable or disassembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can, like, ship off firmware to someone and it's literally like, hey, open this app, upload it

claims.claim_text: Power characterisation is done against a budget rather than by open-ended measurement: the current in each system state, such as modem transmitting, modem sleeping and the Bluetooth microcontroller idle, is estimated at design time, and measurement then checks each state against the estimate.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can kind of work up a budget
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth asset tag keeps per-device cost and power low by only broadcasting a beacon identifier; the location fix comes from passing phones that report the sighting with their own GPS, so utility depends on how many phones pass the tag.
claims.quote_verbatim: you keep the per device cost down because, you know, Bluetooth chips are cheap

claims.claim_text: A national COVID contact-tracing application that relied on Bluetooth advertising in the background failed on Apple devices, illustrating that background Bluetooth operation is governed by the handset platform rather than by the Bluetooth specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: it doesn't actually work on Apple devices

claims.claim_text: The nRF52810 is the low end of the nRF52 family and the nRF52840 the high end; the low-end part with a coin cell is cheap enough to appear in single-use disposable products.
claims.quote_verbatim: That is the low, that's the low end of that, of that family

claims.claim_text: Thread is a mesh arrangement built on the 802.15.4 radio protocol at 2.4 GHz, which lets the same class of low-power node used for Bluetooth carry routed traffic instead of a point-to-point link.
claims.quote_verbatim: Thread is basically like a meshing protocol built on top of 802.15.4

claims.claim_text: A point-to-point Bluetooth radio is the wrong primitive for a gateway that must collect from many low-power sensors and backhaul over cellular; a mesh layer is what makes that platform work.
claims.quote_verbatim: point-to-point Bluetooth like that wouldn't have been the right option
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An nRF52840 is nominally a Bluetooth part but its radio can carry other 2.4 GHz protocols, which is what allows the same silicon to be used for Thread meshing.
claims.quote_verbatim: which is normally like a Bluetooth chip, but it can do other types of 2.4 gigahertz radios

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth peripheral has no publicly routable IP address; it holds a local address on the phone it is paired with, and the phone translates between the internet and the Bluetooth link. Thread nodes instead receive an IPv6 address through a border router and are addressable from the wider internet.
claims.quote_verbatim: there is usually not a publicly addressable IP address on that thing

claims.claim_text: An air-quality sensor was given two data paths: Bluetooth Low Energy for live retrieval by a phone during exercise, and NFC so the data could be downloaded by touch afterwards without carrying the phone. The sensor measured 18 by 18 by 8 millimetres and weighed about five grams, with the battery carried separately in the garment.
claims.quote_verbatim: we'll make this information available through bluetooth low energy
claims.speaker: Andrea Longobardi
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: The low-cost nRF52810 pairs a Cortex-M4 with an integrated Bluetooth radio, runs at about 32 microamps per megahertz with roughly two microamps per megahertz more when executing from flash rather than RAM, and works down to 1.7 volts.
claims.quote_verbatim: It can run at 32 microamps per meg

claims.claim_text: A 2.4 GHz product need not use Bluetooth at all: a proprietary link with a unique 128-bit encryption key programmed into each unit at the factory removes channel setup entirely and eliminates the pairing step.
claims.quote_verbatim: each one comes factory program with its own unique in encryption out of the box

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth's practical throughput ceiling of about one megabit per second or less rules it out for pushing display content or video to a device, forcing the design to Wi-Fi and an order-of-magnitude increase in power consumption.
claims.quote_verbatim: having a practical limit of one megabit per second or less for throughput
claims.speaker: Aedan Cullen
claims.episode_title: Building AR Headsets with Aedan Cullen

claims.claim_text: There is no satisfactory low-power personal-area network between Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, so a design needing more than Bluetooth's data rate has no intermediate option; video has been carried over Bluetooth by exploiting efficiencies in the specification, but it remains low bandwidth.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's not really a very satisfying low power personal area network
claims.speaker: Aedan Cullen
claims.episode_title: Building AR Headsets with Aedan Cullen

claims.claim_text: Consumer Bluetooth Low Energy appliances commonly broadcast their state with no key exchange, so any receiver in range can decode the activity; a mains toothbrush was found to advertise its usage openly and be readable by a generic home automation integration.
claims.quote_verbatim: There was no like key exchange

claims.claim_text: Practical Bluetooth range indoors is short and highly dependent on construction: a beacon may be readable across a small house while other Bluetooth devices fail to penetrate a single interior wall.
claims.quote_verbatim: Most of my Bluetooth stuff can't even get through a single wall

claims.claim_text: The SIG defines standard GATT profiles for common device classes such as a health thermometer or a heart rate monitor, so a generic host can decode those packets without device-specific code; the set reflects the applications anticipated early in the protocol's life and has grown since.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like a standardized packet

claims.claim_text: For its first decade Bluetooth was in practice a wireless audio link plus a few simple gadgets, many of which used the ANT protocol instead; Bluetooth Low Energy arrived in 2010 and brought the low-power and longer-range branches of the standard.
claims.quote_verbatim: Bluetooth low energy was 2010 was Bluetooth low energy

claims.claim_text: If a device continually publishes its readings in a standard GATT message, a listener can decode them without pairing; where pairing is required, the host must negotiate with each device before any data is available.
claims.quote_verbatim: Then you don't have to pair with it

claims.claim_text: A long-range mesh node splits the two radios by role: an ESP32 presents a Bluetooth interface to the phone application while a Semtech LoRa transceiver carries the long-distance link, with the mesh forwarding up to three hops.
claims.quote_verbatim: the ESP32 sets up as a Bluetooth interface

claims.claim_text: The 2.4 GHz band carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and assorted IoT protocols including Thread, and is congested; the mitigation available to product designers is band diversity, using 5 GHz or the newer Wi-Fi generations where the application allows.
claims.quote_verbatim: 2.4 is quite a mess
claims.speaker: Katerina Galitskaya
claims.episode_title: All About Antennas with Katerina Galitskaya

claims.claim_text: A board combining an ESP32-C3 with an nRF9160 spans GPS, LTE and 2.4 GHz, which means three bands and three antenna problems; a common practice is to fit a UFL or SMA connector and delegate the antenna design rather than integrate it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I put a, you know, an SMA connector or a UFL connector on there
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: All About Antennas with Katerina Galitskaya

claims.claim_text: A true Bluetooth beacon transmits its data unsolicited and periodically for any listener to receive, which is distinct from advertising in preparation for pairing; asset trackers generally sit in beacon mode.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's like a true beacon where it's just, Hey, the temperature is 23
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth data-logging link produced a failure worse than a dropout: a fixed one-volt reading was reported as ten volts, a value outside the range the meter was set to, so corruption in the link was indistinguishable from a real measurement. A dropout reported as a null value would have been benign.
claims.quote_verbatim: If there's a genuine dropout, like, tell me it's a dropout
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Diagnosing intermittent corruption over a Bluetooth link means isolating each element of the chain in turn: the instrument, the firmware in the Bluetooth module, the Bluetooth driver on the receiving handset, and the handset operating system version.
claims.quote_verbatim: Which version of Android is it running? Which version of Bluetooth driver is it running?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In CVSS risk scoring the attack vector is ranked remote, then local, then adjacent, then physical; attacks over a radio protocol such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi fall in the adjacent category, which scores lower than a network-reachable Linux device with an IP address.
claims.quote_verbatim: some kind of RF based protocol, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi kind of all falls in that category

claims.claim_text: Low-power Bluetooth systems meet their energy budget in two ways: an extremely small duty cycle in which the RF circuits are live only briefly and off for well over 95 percent of the time, with a background digital controller running between bursts, and optimisation of the power drawn by what remains.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're basically off for 95% of the time or even more
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: Some IoT standards for house-wide mesh networks mandate a minimum battery life of one or two years, because replacing cells in dozens of nodes at short intervals is not acceptable to the user.
claims.quote_verbatim: They mandate that the battery life must be two years or a year
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: A board-level design using a bare CSR Bluetooth chip instead of a module was chosen to save roughly eight dollars a unit, a module costing about ten dollars against one to two dollars for the chip, and cost about eight months porting an open-source Bluetooth stack to it.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was like $10 for a module instead of $1 for, you know, or $2 for the Bluetooth chip
claims.speaker: Eric Migicovsky
claims.episode_title: Shiny New Pebble with Eric Migicovsky

claims.claim_text: The early-stage bill of materials should be optimised for the least hassle in shipping a first product rather than for mass-production cost, because the purpose of the first units is to establish that the product is worth building at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to optimize it for what's the least hassle before I can ship this product
claims.speaker: Eric Migicovsky
claims.episode_title: Shiny New Pebble with Eric Migicovsky

claims.claim_text: Choosing a silicon vendor whose part is natively supported by Zephyr supplies a maintained Bluetooth stack with the kernel, and the alternative is keeping the existing RTOS and integrating a separate open-source stack; the cost of each path is hard to forecast in advance.
claims.quote_verbatim: which would give us the Bluetooth stack, you know, for free or whatever
claims.speaker: Eric Migicovsky
claims.episode_title: Shiny New Pebble with Eric Migicovsky

claims.claim_text: A shipped embedded product's Bluetooth connection continued to work with subsequent Android and iOS releases for eight years after the last unit was manufactured, indicating that host-side Bluetooth compatibility can be durable where the device has few external dependencies.
claims.quote_verbatim: the Bluetooth connection to subsequent Android and iOS versions kept working for eight years after that
claims.speaker: Eric Migicovsky
claims.episode_title: Shiny New Pebble with Eric Migicovsky

claims.claim_text: The prevailing mental model of Bluetooth as a very short-range link derives from its origin as a high-fidelity audio streaming standard; from a purely RF standpoint nothing in the physical layer restricts it to that use.
claims.quote_verbatim: from a pure RF perspective, there's no reason it has to just be that use case
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro

claims.claim_text: A Bluetooth chip can be treated simply as a source of 2.4 GHz sine waves and driven to emit a custom waveform rather than run the Bluetooth stack, which makes a satellite uplink a software-only change to an existing device.
claims.quote_verbatim: We can use the Bluetooth chip and instead emit our own waveform in the 2.4 gigahertz band
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth chips transmit at between zero and 20 dBm, so a link over hundreds of kilometres has to be closed at the receiver: lowering the bit rate puts more energy into each bit, and thousands of antennas performing digital beamforming on the satellite form narrow spot beams that isolate one weak transmitter from the rest.
claims.quote_verbatim: they have to operate between zero to 20 dBm output
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro

claims.claim_text: Bluetooth was preferred over LoRa as the device-side radio because Bluetooth is already embedded in nearly every electronic product, whereas LoRa silicon is available only from Semtech.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can only get your chip from Semtech
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro

claims.claim_text: Two waveforms can share one Bluetooth chip because an advertising device is idle most of the time: a tag advertising every two seconds transmits for under a hundred milliseconds and leaves about 1.9 seconds free. A chip can only emit one waveform at a time, so continuous audio streaming has to be paused for the second transmission.
claims.quote_verbatim: those are very short, uh, sub hundred millisecond advertisements
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro
